text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
+IPE Brent faces resistance first at $18.96 a barrel, a recent high on the continuation chart. Support lies at $18.46-$18.48.
+Gas oil faces resistance at recent highs at $168 a tonne.

IPE Brent crude oil futures were expected to open lower and support for the September contract lies first at $18.45-$18.48, the level of recent highs on the continuation chart and of a falling trendline which was resistance until Thursday.
September Brent closed 29 cents a barrel firmer on Thursday at $18.69 a barrel, after gas oil ended $3.25 up at $167.
"The important number to the upside is $18.96," said Tony Machachek at Credit Lyonnais Rouse in London. This number is the high point reached on the front month continuation chart on July 2.
He said that on the way to $18.96 the market was likely to find some resistance too, at Thursday's high of $18.79.

Support was currently lying in wait at around $18.48, which not only corresponds approximately to the highs of Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday of this week, but also reflects a falling trendline from May which formed resistance earlier in the week, was broken on Thursday, and now constitutes support.

Nicholas Wilson at MeesPierson Derivatives in the Isle of Man saw a similar picture. "In the short term we could see a bit more work (on the upside). But I a looking for the rally to fail. The overall trend is still down."

Looking at the September chart, he placed resistance in the $19.00-$19.05 region. The latter number is the 50 percent retracement of the move from the highs in late May down to the low on June 20, and the former number is the high point reached on July 2.
He pegged resistance for gas oil at $169.50, the July 3 high on the August contract chart, followed by $171, the 50 percent retracement from the full downwards move from late May.
"The rally should fail there," he said, adding next important support lay down at $160.
"I am looking for that to be broken in the next couple of weeks and that will take us down to $150.50.
Machachek, looking at gas oil's continuation chart, saw important resistance at the recent high of $168. "That is quite a crucial number," he said, and pegged support at $165.25 and $163.50.
